title: [finding] the swallow-family census's DETERMINED row for keys.ts still says the site is waiting for a FAILURE_PROPAGATION_SITES declaration the ruling refused
body:
Sub-issue of #15459, which enumerates three statements in the census header that went stale when the #12981 handover landed. This is a **fourth stale statement in the same file, outside the header** — found while landing #12981 batch 10b (PR #15472), which deletes the identical promise from the site itself.

`scripts/measure-durability-swallow-family.mjs`, the `DETERMINED` register row for `packages/runtime/src/domains/keys.ts::handleKeysRequest`, still ends its `why` with:

> ⛔ The declaration this site is waiting for belongs to the programme's LAST step, the one that widens `DURABILITY_CRITICAL_CALLEES`; this row does not bring that step forward and must not be re-keyed by it.

The ruling on #12981 (comment 5543738972, **Q1 = A**) settles that no such declaration is owed at that site, ever: the sanctioned widening added `tryInsert` / `tryUpdate`, neither of which matches a seam in `handleKeysRequest`, and the only name that would match is bare `insert`, which this census refuses by design. An entry keyed there would be STALE on arrival. So the site is not "waiting for" anything — the register row **is** the record, which is exactly what the ruling relies on.

**Scope of the repair:** prose in one `why` string. The row's `anchor`, `verdict`, `scope` and key are correct and must not move — the anchor is cross-checked against the file on every run, and PR #15472 keeps that sentence byte-identical for precisely this reason.

⛔ Not a behaviour defect: the census reading, its `--self-test` (`3 DETERMINED register row(s) cross-check clean`) and its controls are green and unchanged by #15472 (reading byte-identical before and after, `diff` exit 0).

Why filed rather than fixed in batch 10b: that card's surface is one comment in `packages/runtime/src/domains/keys.ts`, and this instrument is the shared measurement device of the same programme — the same reason #15459 was filed rather than repaired in-batch. Duplicate check: 561 open issues enumerated by page over the repo-scoped REST list endpoint (591 total open items, matching `open_issues_count`) and grepped locally, plus one directed semantic search including closed cards; no match. Unassigned.
